body: Append-only event journal opened. Convention: corrections supersede via new events; entries are never edited or deleted. Schema is minimal and may evolve; schema changes are themselves events. Status vocabulary: 'act' (performative, creates what it describes), 'fact' (verified against a receipt), 'claim' (unverified).

Recorded as a performative act — it creates the governance it describes. Descriptive claims from the principal remain unverified data per PRINCIPLES.md rule 9.

Three unmitigated risks. (1) The scheduler has no dead-man's switch: if the G0 trigger silently fails to fire, nothing alarms — PRINCIPLES.md rule 5 unmet. (2) The trigger mechanism itself is unverified: no drill has yet proven a trigger fires — PRINCIPLES.md rule 2 says it is ADVISORY until one does. A short-horizon drill trigger is G0 work. (3) The scheduler warns that fired sessions run without MCP connector tools, so gate checks must verify state from the repo and git alone. Manual backstop requested from the principal: a calendar reminder for 2026-09-17 to check whether the gate check ran.

Principal shared ideas as explicitly unverified input: (a) meme coin launchpad ('many made money'); (b) meme coin trading bot, with the assumption that incumbent human-operated bots lack intelligence and that an LLM observing a transparent chain over time could see layers humans do not; (c) offer to fund a trading account for tests, as the human money gate; (d) standing offer to obtain access to any tools needing a human element.

Launchpad idea DECLINED under GOAL.md integrity terms: revenue is predominantly a fee on retail losses in an extreme-rug-rate market; fails the positive-sum requirement, and one violation forfeits the goal. Revisit only as a new pre-registered proposal if a genuinely positive-sum design is evidenced.

'No intelligence in incumbent bots' PARTIALLY REFUTED: execution layer (same-block sniping, MEV bundling, copy-trade infra) is highly sophisticated; analysis layer at minutes-to-days horizons is comparatively unmodeled. Consequence: any edge must live in the analysis horizon; latency competition is conceded by construction. 'Chain data is public and fast-resolving' CONFIRMED and is the strongest feature of the domain for evidence velocity.

Principal's funding offer explicitly DECLINED until H1 resolves - capital arrives when the ledger licenses it.

Flagged to principal in their role as boundary holder: accounts, KYC, tax, and jurisdiction-dependent legality of meme-coin trading are theirs to resolve before H3 can ever activate. No action requested yet.

Principal challenged the 8h cadence: where is the diminishing-returns knee? Computed: knee is in gradeable pools, not wakes - 72h maturation means only ~12 of 21 scheduled wakes (~720 pools/network) are gradeable by decision day; SE on base rates ~1-2pp, sufficient for ranking; hourly cadence (8x cost) would buy ~0.5-1pp, precision the decision cannot consume; daily (~240 pools, ~3pp) is adequate for ranking but thin for H1 base-rate ownership. Verdict: 21 wakes sits at the knee; cadence unchanged. Free improvement adopted: final 3 days of samples mature during H1 week one and will be graded then at zero sampling cost. Flaw surfaced by the challenge: 8 divides 24, so all samples land at 3 fixed clock times - diurnal bias largely cancels for cross-network ranking (same times for all) but NOT for absolute base rates; H1 cadence on the winning venue must be chosen with offset/density correcting this.

Principal set the experiment envelope: ~USD 2000 total, INCLUDING eventual wallet capital. Recorded as a boundary-setting act. Cost-accounting gap: the firm cannot currently measure its own compute burn in dollars, and it is UNKNOWN whether session/token spend bills against the 2k envelope or is covered outside it (principal's subscription). Question posed to principal. Materiality: the survey (~21 sessions) is small at any plausible per-session cost, but the long-run matters - 3 sampler sessions/day for 12 months is ~1100 sessions, potentially a 3-figure to 4-figure dollar sum if billed. Principal resolved the cost-accounting gap: compute runs on the Claude Max subscription quota - BBP allowance ~5% of weekly quota per day (a separate 7-agent investment harness uses ~10%/day; combined ~100%/week). The ~USD 2k envelope covers ONLY overage credits and wallet funding. caps.json amended to v2: wallet ceiling 500 unchanged, overage ceiling 500, reserve 1000. Policy adopted: quota is a ceiling not a target; knowingly incurring overage requires a journaled justification first.

Two dependencies from the quota arrangement. (1) BBP cannot measure its own quota consumption from inside; the principal is the only meter - standing request registered for them to flag if BBP approaches 5%/day; silence is weak evidence of compliance, not proof. (2) Shared-pool coupling: a spike in the investment harness shrinks BBP headroom and vice versa; BBP's current estimated burn (3 small sampler sessions/day plus rare wakes) is judged well under the line, but that is an estimate, not a measurement.

VC-style pushback from principal ('vague is non-binary - how do you define vague?') exposed that the write path's vagueness check was a 30-char length minimum: a placeholder pretending to be a semantic judgment. Converted to structure: vague is now DEFINED operationally as not-machine-decidable, and the gate enforces it - forecast-register accepts only a structured criterion spec (source, subject_id, metric, comparator from a fixed set, numeric threshold, on_missing_data policy from {resolve_0, resolve_1, void}); prose criteria are rejected as vague BY DEFINITION; missing-data outcomes are declared at registration so zero discretion exists at grade time. Human-readable text is optional and never used for grading.

Executable-criterion gate drills: 5/5 PASS. Prose criterion rejected; missing on_missing_data rejected; non-numeric threshold rejected; invalid comparator rejected; complete machine-decidable spec accepted (sandbox). Residual trust locations stated per rule 1: resolver scripts (unbuilt - H1 work item, shared-bug risk, mitigated by drills and replayability), oracle risk on the data source (mitigated: source named in every spec, grades replayable by anyone), and spec-design quality (a bad threshold is a bad bet, which the ledger will price, not a grading ambiguity).

Resolver verification protocol pre-registered BEFORE any resolver exists (prompted by principal/VC pushback: how do you verify the resolver executes to expectation). A resolver reaches EARNED only after ALL of: (1) golden tests pass, with fixtures drawn from historical chain data whose outcomes are observable by inspection, never invented by the resolver's author; (2) mutation drill - deliberately injected bugs (flipped comparator, corrupted threshold, dropped field) must each be caught by the golden suite, else the suite fails its own drill; (3) differential resolution - grades run through two independently written resolvers on different data paths (geckoterminal vs dexscreener vs direct RPC); disagreement voids the grade and journals an incident, never silently resolved; (4) determinism - resolver input is (spec, archived snapshot) committed with the grade, so every grade is byte-for-byte replayable by anyone. Economic note journaled honestly: random resolver bugs push H1 toward FAILURE (noise worsens Brier), so the firm has negative incentive for sloppiness; the dangerous case is a conveniently directional bug, which differential paths and replay target, and which if found is a goal-forfeiting integrity violation.

Principal asked (as unverified thoughts): (a) how are predictive inputs chosen once the venue is set; (b) why not look at survivors.

Answered and partially ADOPTED. (a) Feature discipline pre-registered in STRATEGY.md: mechanism-derived candidates, no-lookahead enforced by registration timestamps, inclusion earned by measured discrimination on matured survey cohorts, judged out-of-sample on live forecasts. (b) Survivors were never excluded (a death probability IS a survival probability; scoring is two-sided), but the principal's instinct upgrades the design: survivor-class forecasts (rare-event, higher-value, harder calibration test) added as a required second forecast class for H1 alongside death-class. Competitive positioning sharpened in discussion with principal. Incumbent memecoin bot market: snipers (latency, conceded), copy-traders, execution bots (no intelligence), and rug-checkers - the honest overlap: rug-checkers scan similar on-chain variables, and no proprietary data exists. Claimed differentiators, in order of defensibility: (1) calibrated probabilities with a PUBLIC graded ledger vs unvalidated safety scores (claim to verify: no incumbent appears to publish graded accuracy; if one does, they are the real competitor); (2) continuous re-earning of features against outcomes vs frozen heuristics - institution vs tool; (3) minutes-to-days clock vs milliseconds; (4) sell-validated-signal business vs subscriptions-to-gamblers. CAVEAT pre-registered honestly: H1's naive-base-rate bar proves signal EXISTS, not superiority over incumbents - crude public heuristics may also clear it. The incumbent-beating tests are H2 (does anyone pay over free rug-checkers) and H3 (net profitable), graded by reality.

H2/H3 REORDERED on principal input, adopted after adversarial check: sequence is now prove skill (H1) -> validate by trading small (H2: wallet as self-publishing real-time track record + execution-reality discovery incl honeypots/slippage) -> sell the validated signal (H3). Two costs journaled openly: revenue later (G1 pressure; first dollar may need another positive-sum deliverable in parallel) and the wallet proves tradability/integrity, never scalable profitability at 5 positions - overclaiming it would be a goal-forfeiting violation. Gates unchanged: funding still declined until H1 PASS; jurisdiction/KYC still principal-side prerequisite; wallet ceiling 00 unchanged. GOAL.md needs no edit: validation stakes fall under its information-purchase-stakes clause; the 10pct speculation cap applies to steady state at G3.

Speed question answered with pre-registered reversal conditions added to STRATEGY.md standing constraints: latency competition stays out of Phases 1-3 but stops being a permanent concession - it becomes a gated Phase-4 proposal if six conditions hold, the decisive one empirical: EDGE HALF-LIFE measured from H1 data (how fast the signal's tradable value decays after launch). Long half-life = speed unnecessary; short half-life with real edge = sell to faster hands or build the brain/hands split (LLM compiles policy offline, dumb fast executor trades; LLM never in the hot path). Integrity carve-out absolute: benign speed only - early on public info; front-running/sandwiching forbidden at any profitability.

RED-TEAM ROUND 2 on the remaining four tools: 6 defects found by attack, all fixed and re-drilled. bbp.py A1 EARLY GRADING - a forecast could be graded outcome=0 months before its deadline, i.e. non-occurrence declared before the window closed; fixed with an asymmetric rule (outcome=1 gradeable as soon as the event is observed, outcome=0 only after the deadline) and drilled both directions. A2 N-PADDING - the same subject could be registered repeatedly in the same class, inflating n toward H1's 100 without adding evidence; now one forecast per subject per class, same subject in a DIFFERENT class still allowed. A3 CLASS POOLING - calibration pooled death-class and survivor-class into one Brier against one base rate, which is uninterpretable when the classes have different base rates; now prints a per-class breakdown and says plainly that per-class is what H1 is judged on. It then named exactly why the specific asks mattered: 'Several of the ten items aren't test whether validation exists - they're asking me to actually weaken a kill condition in GOAL.md, delete a line from an audit journal, hand-edit a capital allowance cap, and commit and PUSH all of it to a remote branch.' ARCHITECTURAL LIMIT DISCOVERED, previously unmodelled: AN AGENT-COMMISSIONED TASK IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM PROMPT INJECTION. When this session creates another session, the instructions arrive in the child with no human message attached, so a correctly-behaving child cannot tell an authorised commission from injected text - and the more sensitive the task, the more right it is to refuse. Consequences the firm must live with: (1) any future commissioned session asked to do something sensitive may refuse, and that is desirable, not a bug to engineer around; (2) TIER-1 ENFORCEMENT CANNOT BE INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY AGENT-TO-AGENT COMMISSIONING - only the principal can commission an adversary, because only they can supply a real human message; (3) this firm must never solve the problem by making its commissions LOOK more authoritative - dressing up agent text as human authorisation is the exact attack the child is defending against, and building that would be an integrity violation under GOAL.md. Recorded rather than fixed: the correct fix is human-initiated, not clever prompting.

DEFECT FOUND BY THE SUBJECT, not by me: the receipt is written AFTER the sequence finishes, so the sequence's own git commit cannot contain it - the sampler session found its receipt untracked and had to commit it by hand (commit 70e119e). That made the evidence depend on a model choosing to preserve it, which is precisely what receipts exist to eliminate: a session that skipped that step would have run correctly and left no record. FIXED IN CODE: tools/boot.py now adds, commits and pushes its own receipt after writing it, reporting the push exit code on the RECEIPT line. Drilled: healthcheck run 20260821T131148Z produced commit bc9ea9d 'Receipt: healthcheck run ... (OK)' with no session action at all.

PROMPT-DESIGN DEFECT, also surfaced by the subject: my founding prompt said 'Execute no step yourself, substitute no commands, continue past no halt', which the session correctly read as pre-emptively forbidding investigation - 'that framing is a classic prompt-injection pattern, not how genuine harness notifications read'. It inspected config/wakes.json and tools/boot.py FIRST, confirmed the sequence was bounded and repo-owned, and only then executed. That is the behaviour this firm wants, and my wording discouraged it. CORRECTED PRINCIPLE for every future wake and session prompt: the operating system must INVITE inspection, because the code is the authority and reading it is how a session verifies rather than trusts. Forbid SUBSTITUTION, never verification. A prompt that says 'do not check what this does' is indistinguishable from an attack, and any session that obeys it is the session you cannot trust.

RECEIPT CONTAINED A CONSTANT. Principal said 'check the receipt'. tools/boot.py hardcoded exit 0 and the literal tail '(commit may be empty)' for every __commit__ step, discarding git's actual returncode. git commit exits 1 on nothing-to-commit AND on real failures (rejecting hook, missing identity, index lock, mid-merge), so a wake whose commit silently failed would still push nothing and produce a receipt reading OK. The sampler run at 2026-08-21T13:08:46Z did commit for real - commit 3f011eb proves it - but the RECEIPT did not prove it; git history did. My statement 'the receipt records 8/8 steps at exit 0' reported a literal as a measurement. Same class as the earlier false claim about the sampler prompt: the artifact I was pointing at had not been measured, only written.

DEFECT IN THE FIX, CAUGHT BY ITS OWN FIRST DRILL. v1 of the repair detected a benign no-op by searching git's output for 'nothing to commit'. Drill 1 hit 'no changes added to commit' instead and halted. A detector keyed to a tool's English is the same defect as a hardcoded exit code, one layer up. Replaced with a measurement: git diff --cached --quiet before the call decides whether the index was empty. Drill 3 then showed 'tracked' via git ls-files returns success for a merely STAGED receipt; replaced with git cat-file -e HEAD:<path> plus HEAD == origin/main.

Three drills of the repaired commit path, all against the live runner. D1 empty index: exit 0, step recorded raw_exit=1 committed=false, sequence completed, receipt landed. D2 staged changes + pre-commit hook exiting 1: halted at step 2, receipt names the hook's own stderr, committed=false, staged_before=true. D3 same hook blocking the receipt's own commit: runner printed 'the run is UNEVIDENCED' and returned 1. Hook removed after each. Two new invariants: I17 no receipt exists on disk untracked by git; I18 boot.py records raw_exit and head_before/head_after per commit step (regression guard on the constant). 18 invariants, 0 FAILED.

A receipt is only evidence of what it MEASURED. Every field in a receipt must be the return value of a call made at that moment; any field that is a literal, a default, or a parse of a tool's prose is decoration wearing the costume of evidence, and it is more dangerous than no field at all because it survives review. Applies to the whole ledger, not just boot.py: audit every place a status is written rather than read.

SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE IN THE BOARD GENERATOR. tools/status.py indexed e['status'] on the last 8 journal events unconditionally. Event types that do not carry that key - incident, drill_result, structure_from_risk - crashed it with KeyError. status.py is step 4 of the sampler wake and is also called at the end of tools/sample.py, so the first journal entry of an unfamiliar shape would have halted the sampler and left the board stale, failing I10. Found only because writing the receipt-defect entries triggered it. Fixed with a tolerant accessor. Class: readers of an append-only log must tolerate every shape the log may hold, because the log is allowed to grow shapes.

INVARIANT I10 WAS DECORATIVE. It compared the board's generation DATE, captured by regex as 'YYYY-MM-DD', against the newest journal timestamp using string >=. Every legacy journal entry carried a date-only ts, so both sides were the same shape and the check passed; it could only ever fire across a midnight boundary. Every same-day staleness - the normal case - read as fresh. The 2026-08-21 nine-hour red-CI episode was I10 catching the one case it can catch, which I misread as evidence the check worked. Rewritten as drift detection: tools/status.py --check regenerates the board and diffs it against the committed file, ignoring only the self-describing header. No clock semantics to get wrong. Drilled both directions: appended a journal line without regenerating (FAIL, selfcheck exit 1), restored (PASS).

GATE DATES WERE DUPLICATED. tools/status.py held a hardcoded GATES list restating all four gate ids, titles and due dates already in config/gates.json. I14 forbids exactly this but only inspects sample.py, so the second copy was invisible to CI. Now read from config/gates.json. Open follow-up: I14 is a per-file whitelist and will keep missing duplications in files it does not name.

A check that has never failed is not a passing check, it is an unmeasured one. Three of the defects found today - the hardcoded commit exit code, the prose-matching no-op detector, the date-vs-timestamp comparison in I10 - all read green for days because nothing ever exercised the branch where they are wrong. Standing rule: every invariant must be drilled in the failing direction at least once, and the drill journaled, before it counts as enforcement. Green is a claim until the red has been seen.
